Quiero crear una página web personal que sirva a modo de "porfolio" para un periodista de tecnología con más de una década de experiencia. La página web debe tener un estilo minimalista, elegante y "pixel perfect", con elementos de diseño de 2025 tales como gradientes y efecto "liquid glass", pero sin resultar excesivo. La página web dará la bienvenida al visitante con una descripción del periodista usando el siguiente texto: 

"¡Hola!
Soy Christian

Director de Andro4all, medio sobre Android, tecnología y telefonía móvil líder en español, integrado en el periódico La Vanguardia entre 2023 y 2025. Actualmente, Andro4all es el vertical de tecnología de consumo del periódico La Razón.

Soy Técnico superior en desarrollo de aplicaciones multiplataforma, con experiencia en desarrollo web y apps Android.
Escribo noticias de actualidad, analizo productos y doy mi opinión sobre la industria tecnológica desde hace más de 9 años. Hasta hoy, he publicado más de 12.000 artículos. También hago fotos, puedes verlas en mi perfil de Flickr o en mi cuenta de Instagram.

Si quieres contactar conmigo, puedes hacerlo a través de Bluesky, X, Threads o por correo electrónico."

Después de la presentación, habrá un carrusel de noticias que se extraerá del siguiente feed RSS: https://andro4all.com/author/christian-collado/feed

Este carrusel mostrará las últimas 5 noticias publicadas.

**Crafting a Portfolio**

I'm currently fleshing out the structure for Christian's portfolio. Focusing on a bio, an RSS feed carousel, and contact links as core elements. Trying to embody a 2025 minimalist aesthetic, leaning heavily on gradients and liquid glass. Aiming for pixel-perfect design.


**Refining Technical Implementation**

I'm now diving into the technical details. React 18+ and TypeScript are my go-to choices, along with Tailwind CSS for rapid styling.  For the RSS feed, I'll attempt a public proxy first, then explore an AI-driven fetcher to pull and summarize content, given the project requirements.  The Gemini API will add some interactive "Tech Insight" sections to make this stand out. My plan is to start with a metadata file and progressively implement the major components and services. I'm choosing Inter for the typography and a palette that contains deep grays/blacks with vibrant indigo and violet gradients.


**Designing Visuals & Functionality**

I'm now focusing on the visual elements. Large headlines, subtle borders, and liquid glass effects are a priority. I'll use `https://api.rss2json.com/v1/api.json?rss_url=` to get the RSS feed. The hero section will feature a big "¡Hola! Soy Christian". The carousel will use `framer-motion` for a smooth, modern scroll. I'll include links to Bluesky, X, Threads, and email with icons from Lucide-react. The bio will be in Spanish and there will be a carousel with the last 5 articles. The Liquid Glass will be `bg-white/10 backdrop-blur-md border border-white/20`.


**Constructing Project Files**

I'm presently building out the project's foundational structure. I'm focusing on key files like `metadata.json`, `index.html`, and the core React components. The file structure is being meticulously laid out. I'm meticulously confirming the functionality: RSS feed handling, minimalist aesthetic, accurate social links, precise bio text, and the projected "2025" design elements with mesh gradients and glassmorphism. I'm using `rss2json` as a proxy to address potential CORS issues with the RSS feed URL.

I'm experimenting with less complex gradients, potentially a deep navy/charcoal for better contrast, or perhaps a completely light theme.

I'm now focusing on readability. The feedback about white text on dark backgrounds has prompted a significant shift. I'm leaning towards a very dark navy or charcoal instead of pure black for improved contrast. I'm also considering a simplified, less distracting gradient, or a solid color background. It seems a less complex approach is key to improving readability.

I'm keeping the white text as requested, and I'm updating the mesh gradient to be more subtle in its effect. Removing the "Journalist" subtitle is also complete. **Improving Gradient Subtlety**

I've been refining the background and am now minimizing the mesh gradient's impact. I want the gradient to be extremely subtle, localized only to the edges, creating a solid backdrop for content. name: Deploy to GitHub Pages

on:
  push:

payload.text: Hay un problema con el scroll de la web en formato móvil. Arréglalo para que sea más suave y fluido al cargar los diferentes elementos.

**Improving Mobile Scroll Performance**

I'm currently focused on fixing the jerky mobile scroll in the portfolio app. The initial culprit seems to be `scroll-behavior: smooth`, so I'm investigating alternative methods. The goal is buttery-smooth scrolling across all devices. I'll need to research native scrolling solutions. This requires deep diving into browser rendering optimizations, and testing across different device brands and operating systems.


**Pinpointing Scroll Bottlenecks**

I'm now zeroing in on specific performance bottlenecks. My investigation reveals that heavy backdrop filters and gradients in large layouts are taxing mobile GPUs and that the `LiquidCard`'s unoptimized scroll listener is a major culprit for jank. The `ArticleCarousel` may also have snappiness issues, and simultaneous animations could be causing layout shifts. I plan to optimize `LiquidCard` with CSS scroll-driven animations or a more lightweight approach, like `will-change: transform`. An Intersection Observer might be even better.


**Addressing Filter Issues**

I've realized the primary mobile scroll lag culprit is the `backdrop-filter: blur(...)` combined with heavy gradients and parallax in the `LiquidCard`, leading to frequent React updates. So, I'm now optimizing that. I'll attempt using CSS variables for the parallax logic, updated by a global scroll listener, or outright remove it for mobile. I'll also add `will-change: backdrop-filter, transform` to the liquid cards. I'm also considering `overscroll-behavior-y: none;` and ensuring `-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch;` is present. I'll carefully refine the carousel's snap properties as well.


**Implementing Hardware Acceleration**

I'm now focusing on hardware acceleration for the parallax effect. I'll move the parallax logic out of React state and into CSS variables, updating the offset using `IntersectionObserver`. This avoids re-rendering on every scroll. I will also add `transform: translate3d` to the liquid card. I will further refine the snap behavior of the `ArticleCarousel` and add `will-change` hints in both `index.html` and `LiquidCard.tsx`.


**Refining Scroll Smoothness**

I'm now implementing the parallax effect with `requestAnimationFrame` and `transform` for 60fps performance. I'm also addressing the `ArticleCarousel`, leveraging `overflow-x: auto` and `snap-type` for smoother scrolling. I'll update `index.html` for global scroll improvements, `LiquidCard.tsx` for component-level optimization, and `App.tsx` for mobile-specific layout adjustments.

Para mejorar la fluidez del scroll en dispositivos móviles y eliminar el "jank" (tirones) producido por los efectos de cristal y paralaje, vamos a realizar una optimización de rendimiento centrada en la aceleración por hardware y la reducción de re-renderizados innecesarios.

### Especificación de los cambios:

1.  **Optimización de `LiquidCard`**: El componente utilizaba el estado de React (`useState`) para actualizar la posición en cada píxel de scroll, lo que provocaba re-renderizados masivos. Se ha sustituido por **CSS Variables** y un único listener pasivo optimizado, delegando el movimiento a la GPU mediante `translate3d` y `will-change`.
2.  **Aceleración de Capas (GPU)**: Se han añadido propiedades de `will-change` y `backface-visibility` a los elementos con `backdrop-filter` (filtros de fondo), ya que estos son los que más recursos consumen en procesadores móviles.
3.  **Suavizado Global**: En `index.html` se ha añadido `-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch` para asegurar que el scroll inercial de iOS sea perfecto, y se ha ajustado la propiedad `scroll-padding` para que las anclas no queden tapadas por la navegación.
4.  **Refinamiento del Carrusel**: Se ha mejorado el `snap-type` y añadido `will-change: scroll-position` para que el deslizamiento lateral sea instantáneo y sin fricción.
